project: bankapp — the CIE sample project (the playground)
honesty: Every number here was measured by running this sample project's probes under the named tools on the machine that collected it. Nothing is simulated, extrapolated or invented. Where a measurement could not be taken, the artifact says so. Each dataset names the tool, the command shape, and the production tools that would collect the same evidence on a real project.

cpu.honesty: Measured on this machine during this run; the profiler's own bookkeeping adds a little overhead. A different machine or run will give different numbers — that is what honest measurement looks like.
real_world_equivalents: py-spy top / py-spy record (sampling, safe in production)

concurrency.honesty: This is a measured timeline of one run, not a benchmark. overlap = sum of task time / wall time; >1 means threads genuinely ran at the same time on this run.

memory.honesty: tracemalloc only sees allocations made while it is tracing, and tracing slows the program a little. Peak here is this run's peak, not the process's whole life.
real_world_equivalents: Java heap dumps + JFR memory events

deadlock.honesty: The deadlock is real: both threads were captured blocked at the acquire lines, and the cycle was computed from the holds/wants table they wrote before blocking — not declared by hand. A one-off capture proves this run deadlocked; repeated occurrences need production thread-dump monitoring.

race.tool: read-modify-write observation (no sanitizer needed to SEE this one)
race.command: runtime_probes.racing_counter(threads=4), 3 natural trials (50000 each) + 3 widened trials (20000 each, GIL yielded between read and write — disclosed)
race.honesty: Both windows are real concurrent read-add-write with no lock. The natural window may lose nothing on a given run — CPython's switch checks land on the loop backedge — and that is an honest result: races are timing-dependent, so a clean run is NOT proof the race is gone. The widened window yields the GIL between the read and the write (the same window real code leaves open) and is fully disclosed; it reliably loses updates, proving the sequence is not atomic.

coverage.command: python -m coverage run -m pytest test_auth.py -q (inside the sample project)

totals.note: percent covers files the tests actually import; unmeasured files are listed separately below 0 with their reason

coverage.honesty: Line coverage of the sample project's own tests, measured for real. The gaps are the point: test_auth.py covers auth.py only, so payments.py, ui.py and runtime_probes.py were never even imported by a test — they show as 0 with that reason, not as a fake number.
